omitted_tabs.reason: XTDB 2.1.0 has no constraint statements: every table is keyed by _id and has no declared columns (Sql.g4 has no CREATE TABLE)
Indexing is automatic; XTDB 2.1.0 has no index statement
No user partitioning; storage is organised by the engine (xt.trie_stats)
XTDB 2.1.0 has no grants: users authenticate, and the server's authentication rules decide access

gaps.concept: Altering, renaming or dropping a table
gaps.reason: XTDB 2.1.0 has no table statements. A table appears on its first write; ERASE of every document empties it but information_schema still lists it (live, 2026-10-31)

fields.label: Schema
fields.help: A new schema comes into being with its first table. XTDB 2.1.0 lists it through its tables, not in information_schema.schemata.

fields.label: Table name
fields.help: XTDB has no CREATE TABLE: the table is created by writing its first document.

fields.label: First document
fields.help: One row per field. _id is required and identifies the document. Each field becomes a column with the type of its value; later documents may add fields. Integers are written as 64-bit (:i64), as XTDB SQL writes them; a decimal keeps the precision of its value.

options.label: Nested object or list (written as JSON)

fields.label: Valid from
fields.help: Start of the first document's valid time; empty means now.

fields.label: Valid to
fields.help: End of the first document's valid time; empty means open-ended.

fields.label: Columns
fields.help: Read from information_schema.columns: every field any document has had, with XTDB's type. A type shown as [:union ...] lists every type the field has held, including in erased documents (live, 2.1.0). The four temporal columns are kept by XTDB on every table.

notes: Hand-written for providers/xtdb/client.py. Create writes the first document with INSERT (typed by the grid, providers/xtdb/client.py _initial_document); the post-state check reads the document and its columns back.
